drivers.name: BenQ Display
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls BenQ interactive flat panels (BenQ Boards: RM, RP, RE, CP, CM series) and BenQ Smart Signage using BenQ's RS232 & LAN protocol on TCP port 4660 or direct RS-232. Power and screen off, source select, volume, mute and audio EQ, picture values and modes, backlight, color temperature, aspect, remote-key navigation, IR and keypad locks, power save, and a Power On that wakes a standby display over Wake-on-LAN. Polls for status.

help.overview: BenQ Boards (interactive flat panels) and BenQ Smart Signage speaking BenQ's RS232 & LAN protocol. Power, source, audio, picture controls, backlight, locks, and power-save settings. Polls every 30 seconds. Use Screen Off (not Standby) as the automated 'off' for a space: it blanks the backlight while network control stays available. Standby shuts Android down and the LAN control port with it — Power On wakes a standby display over Wake-on-LAN, and works while the display is offline.
help.setup:
1. Network control: connect the display's LAN port, note the IP address from the network settings, and add it here (TCP port 4660). Monitor ID stays 1 for LAN control.
2. Turn the display's Wake-on-LAN setting on so a standby display can be woken remotely.
3. Serial control: connect the RS-232 port. Current BenQ Boards run 115200 8N1 (fixed); older RP panels and Smart Signage run 9600 8N1 — set Baud Rate to match your model.
4. LAN commands only work while the display is on or screen-off (Android running). After Standby, Power On wakes the display over Wake-on-LAN and the connection comes back on its own.
help.connection: A display in standby (Android off) does not answer on the LAN control port. Power On wakes it over Wake-on-LAN (the display's Wake-on-LAN setting must be on and its MAC address known), or use Screen Off instead of Standby so control stays available.

compatible_models.notes: Every listed model has a published BenQ RS232 & LAN (or RS232 command list) guide with this grammar. Other BenQ Boards and Smart Signage (ST / SL / SM / BH series) publish the same Generic RS232/LAN protocol and are expected to work. Function support varies by model; an unsupported command answers a reject the driver ignores. Current BenQ Boards fix the serial baud at 115200; older RP panels and Smart Signage use 9600.

drivers.name: Hisense VIDAA TV
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Hisense VIDAA OS TVs over the TV's embedded MQTT broker (the path the RemoteNOW/VIDAA app uses). Power, volume, input, key passthrough, and PIN pairing.

help.overview:
Hisense VIDAA TVs are controlled over an MQTT broker built into the TV (port 36669), the same way the RemoteNOW phone app works. Enter the TV's IP address, then pair: run 'Request Pairing' (a 4-digit PIN appears on the TV), then 'Submit Pairing PIN' with that number. The pairing is remembered across restarts.

Power On over the network is best-effort: a TV in deep standby turns its broker off, so it may be unreachable until switched on with the physical remote. Power Off and everything else work while the TV is on.
help.setup:
1. Make sure the TV and OpenAVC are on the same network.
2. On the TV, enable mobile-app/remote control if it has such a setting (Settings > System > Mobile App / 'RemoteNOW').
3. Enter the TV's IP address and save.
4. Run 'Request Pairing', read the PIN on the TV, then run 'Submit Pairing PIN'.

Some newer models only accept a connection that presents a client certificate, which OpenAVC does not include. Those TVs stay offline with a TLS error.

drivers.name: LG SICP Display
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls LG commercial displays via SICP over TCP (port 9761). Each Set ID on an RS-232 daisy chain is a display child entity with power, input, volume, mute, screen-off, signal status, picture settings, and panel health. Covers webOS Signage, LED, and OLED commercial series.

help.overview: Controls LG commercial displays using the SICP protocol. One connection can address several displays daisy-chained over RS-232 by Set ID — each appears as a display child entity with power, input, volume, mute, screen blank, signal status, picture settings, and panel health.
help.setup:
1. Connect the display (or the chain's first display) to the network.
2. Default control port is 9761.
3. In each display's OSD (Settings > General), give it a unique Set ID. List those IDs in 'Display Set IDs' — e.g. 1 for a single display, or 1,2,3,4 for a daisy-chained video wall. Enter the IDs exactly as the OSD shows them (decimal); the driver handles the protocol's hex encoding.
4. Route commands to a display by picking it from the Display dropdown; use All Displays On / Off to drive the whole chain at once.

drivers.name: LG webOS TV
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls LG webOS TVs over the SSAP WebSocket protocol with live power/volume/input feedback.

help.overview: Controls LG webOS TVs (2016 and later) over the SSAP WebSocket protocol: power, volume, mute, input and app switching, and on-screen navigation, with live feedback pushed from the TV.
help.setup:
1. Connect the TV to the network.
2. Add the TV here; on first connect a pairing prompt appears on the TV screen — accept it with the remote.
3. For power-on from standby, set the MAC address and enable Wake-on-LAN ('Mobile TV On') in the TV's network settings.
help.connection: On first connection, accept the pairing prompt on the TV screen. A TV in deep standby is unreachable until woken with Wake-on-LAN.

compatible_models.notes: Verified on a 65UN6950ZUA (webOS 4.x). SSAP is common across webOS 3.0+ consumer TVs; navigation buttons and app ids may vary by model/firmware.

drivers.name: Panasonic Professional Display
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Panasonic TH-series professional displays (SQ / EQ / CQ / VF / SF / BQ lines) over the LAN command channel. Power, input, volume, audio / video mute, aspect, and the picture adjustment surface. Speaks both of Panasonic's LAN control protocols (auto-detected) and supports the MD5 challenge authentication, so the display works whichever way its service menu is set.

help.overview: Panasonic professional displays are controlled over TCP port 1024 using one of two LAN control protocols selected in the display's service menu. This driver auto-detects the protocol from the connection greeting, so either setting works. Optional MD5 challenge authentication is tied to the display's Web Control administrator account. The display closes the control connection between commands — this is normal, documented behaviour the driver expects.
help.setup:
1. Connect the display to the network and assign a static IP.
2. Enable network control: [Initial settings] -> [Network settings] -> [Network control] = On. The default command port is 1024 (shown under [LAN settings]).
3. Open the display's Web Control page in a browser. Set or note the Administrator-Authorized password (default username is ``admin1``, default password is ``panasonic``).
4. In OpenAVC, enter the display's IP and the Web Control admin username and password. If the display has no password set (non-protected mode), leave the password field empty.

compatible_models.notes: The command core (power, input, volume, mutes, aspect, picture) is uniform across the TH-series professional line; the SQ2H and EQ2 command lists are identical and CQ1 carries the same core. Per-series variation is which inputs exist — the input picker offers the SQ2H/EQ2 union and free-typed protocol codes pass through for model extras (e.g. CQ1's TV1 tuner input). Unsupported values return ERR2 on the display, logged at debug.

drivers.name: Promethean ActivPanel 10
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls the Promethean ActivPanel 10 and ActivPanel 10 Premium interactive displays over the network (TCP port 5000) or RS-232. Power, sleep and Wake-on-LAN, input select, volume and mute, freeze, blank, touch and remote locks, OPS computer power, picture levels, backlight mode, standby and sleep timers, front-panel button locks and the ePTZ camera. Polls for status.

help.overview: Promethean ActivPanel 10 and 10 Premium interactive displays. Power, input, volume, mute, freeze, blank, touch and remote locks, the OPS computer's power, picture levels and timers. Polls every 15 seconds. Over the network, Power Off puts the panel to Sleep, which turns its network off: it shows offline until Power On wakes it with Wake-on-LAN.
help.setup:
1. Plug a network cable into the panel's own LAN port (not the OPS computer's), and give the panel a static IP address or a DHCP reservation. The address is under Settings > System > Network.
2. OpenAVC must be on the same subnet as the panel: its network control does not cross subnets.
3. Turn on Settings > Power > Wake on LAN, so Power On can wake a sleeping panel.
4. Network control uses TCP port 5000 and needs no username or password.
5. Serial control instead: a straight RS-232 cable to the panel's RS232 port, 9600 baud, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit. Standby and Power On work over serial without Wake-on-LAN.
help.connection: A panel in Sleep does not answer on the network. Power On wakes it with Wake-on-LAN (Settings > Power > Wake on LAN on, and the panel's MAC address known), and the connection comes back on its own. Check that OpenAVC is on the panel's subnet and that the cable is in the panel's LAN port, not the OPS.

compatible_models.notes: ActivPanel 10. Network control on the panel's own LAN port, TCP 5000, or RS-232 at 9600 8N1.
ActivPanel 10 Premium. Same control codes; the camera commands are for the Promethean ePTZ 4K camera in the Premium's camera mount.

drivers.name: Promethean ActivPanel LE
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls the Promethean ActivPanel LE interactive displays over RS-232, on a serial port or through an IP-to-serial bridge. Power, standby and sleep, input select, volume and mute, and the model, serial number and firmware the panel reports. Polls for status.

help.overview: Promethean ActivPanel LE interactive displays, controlled over RS-232. Power (on, standby and sleep), input, volume and mute, and the model, serial number and firmware the panel reports. Polls every 15 seconds. Promethean documents RS-232 control only for the LE: wire it to a serial port on the OpenAVC server, or to an IP-to-serial bridge.
help.setup:
1. Wire the panel's RS232 port, a 9-pin D-sub at the back of the panel on the underside behind the left side. Pin 2 is the panel's receive, pin 3 its transmit and pin 5 ground: the controller's transmit goes to pin 2 and its receive to pin 3.
2. Direct serial: set the Serial Port (for example COM3 on Windows or /dev/ttyUSB0 on Linux). Through a bridge: add the bridge first, then choose Through a bridge in this device's Connection settings and pick the port the panel is wired to.
3. Serial settings: 115200 baud, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit. They are this driver's defaults; through a bridge, OpenAVC applies them to the bridge's port.
4. No username or password is needed.
5. If the panel does not answer with the wiring and settings right, update it to its latest firmware: Promethean notes that some earlier versions do not support every RS-232 command.
help.connection: The panel answers on its RS-232 port only. If it shows offline, check that it has mains power, the wiring (the controller's transmit to pin 2, its receive to pin 3), and the serial settings: 115200 baud, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit. Through a bridge, check that the bridge's own card shows connected.

compatible_models.notes: ActivPanel LE. RS-232 only, 115200 8N1, on the 9-pin port labelled RS232 at the back of the panel (underside, behind the left side).

drivers.name: Samsung MDC Display
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Samsung commercial displays via the MDC (Multiple Display Control) binary protocol over TCP. Each Set ID on the chain is a display child entity with power, volume, mute, input, and picture settings (brightness, contrast, backlight, picture mode, color tone).

help.overview: Controls Samsung commercial displays using the MDC binary protocol. Covers Smart Signage, The Wall, LED, and SMART Signage Platform series. One connection can address several displays daisy-chained by Set ID. Each appears as a display child entity.
help.setup:
1. Connect the display (or the chain's master) to the network.
2. Enable MDC / network control in the display's settings.
3. Default port is 1515.
4. In the display's menu, give each display a unique Set ID (ID). List those IDs in 'Display Set IDs'. Use 1 for a single display, or 1,2,3,4 for a four-panel wall.
5. Route commands to a display by picking it from the Display dropdown; use All Displays On / Off to drive the whole chain at once.

compatible_models.notes: Verified on hardware (firmware T-GFSLE2AKUC-1037.2): power, volume, mute, input, contrast, brightness, backlight, sharpness and picture mode all round-trip. Colour tone (0x3E) is not implemented on this model and is dropped from the poll on its first NAK; colour temperature (0x3F) answers instead. Picture mode accepts calibration and the signage modes 0x20-0x27 only.
Same MDC command set as the verified DM75E, but which commands and which picture modes a model implements varies; unsupported ones are reported rather than silently ignored.

drivers.name: Sharp PN Display (AQUOS BOARD)
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls pre-merger Sharp PN-series commercial displays and AQUOS BOARD interactive displays (PN-L, PN-E, PN-R and related series) using Sharp's 4-character RS-232C/LAN command protocol on TCP port 10008 or direct RS-232. Power, input select, volume, mute, brightness and picture values, audio EQ, screen size, PIP/PbyP, touch enable, control locks, temperature monitoring, and standby-mode configuration. Polls for status. Post-merger Sharp/NEC displays are covered by the Sharp NEC Display driver instead.

help.overview: Pre-merger Sharp PN-series commercial displays and AQUOS BOARD interactive displays. Power, input, audio, picture controls, PIP, touch enable, control locks, and temperature monitoring. Polls every 30 seconds. Keep STANDBY MODE on STANDARD so a standby display stays controllable over the network.
help.setup:
1. Network control: connect the display's LAN port and set RS-232C/LAN SELECT to LAN in the SETUP menu. Add the display's IP address here (TCP data port, default 10008). If a username/password is set in the display's SECURITY settings, enter the same values here; leave blank otherwise.
2. Keep STANDBY MODE set to STANDARD (Monitor menu). LOW POWER standby shuts down LAN/RS-232C control until the display is woken at the panel.
3. Serial control: connect the RS-232C input terminal (straight cable) and set RS-232C/LAN SELECT to RS-232C. Default 38400 8N1 — match the display's BAUD RATE setting. AQUOS BOARD models use a 3.5mm service jack fixed at 38400.
4. RS-232C and LAN control cannot be used simultaneously.
help.connection: A display in LOW POWER standby does not answer on LAN or RS-232C until woken at the panel — set STANDBY MODE to STANDARD (the Standby Mode device setting) so power_on keeps working. The LAN session requires a login; blank credentials are sent when none are configured.

compatible_models.notes: Every listed model's operation manual documents this command table. Other pre-merger Sharp PN-series monitors and AQUOS BOARD models publish the same protocol and are expected to work; input terminals and optional functions (touch, PIP) vary by model, and an unsupported command answers a reject the driver ignores. Current post-merger Sharp/NEC large-format displays use NEC External Control instead — add those with the Sharp NEC Display driver.

drivers.name: Sharp/NEC Display (External Control)
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Sharp/NEC professional large-format displays over the NEC External Control protocol on TCP 7142. Each Monitor ID on the daisy chain is a display child entity with power, input, volume, mutes, picture settings, panel temperature, and self-diagnosis status. Includes a raw opcode escape hatch for the full protocol surface.

help.overview: NEC External Control runs on TCP 7142 (fixed). One connection can address a whole RS-232 daisy chain of displays by Monitor ID — list the IDs and each becomes a display child entity with its own power, input, volume, picture values, temperature, and self-diagnosis status. The protocol requires the controller to pause 15 seconds after a power command (10 after an input change), so commands sent right after those are delayed briefly. Use Get/Set Opcode for protocol features not surfaced as named commands (PIP, OSD, IR lock, gamma, and more).
help.setup:
1. Connect the display's LAN port and give it a fixed IP. External control is always on; port 7142 is fixed.
2. Check the display's Monitor ID in its OSD (MULTI DISPLAY menu). Factory default is 1.
3. For a daisy-chained wall, connect RS-232 OUT to the next display's IN, give each display a unique Monitor ID, and list them all in 'Monitor IDs' (e.g. 1,2,3,4).
4. Values changed over the protocol are volatile until stored — run Save Settings after commissioning changes.

compatible_models.notes: The G2-generation External Control manual (Rev.2.4) this driver was built from documents these series. Opcode availability varies by model; unsupported opcodes answer result code 01 and the driver stops polling them on that display.

Newer NEC and Sharp-era large-format series publish the same External Control protocol per model (framing, check code, power procedure and core opcodes verified identical in the Exx8-series manual). Expected to work unchanged; not tested on hardware.

drivers.name: SMART Board RX / MX
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: SMART Board RX and MX (V2 to V5) interactive displays over RS-232: power, input, volume and mute, brightness, freeze, screen shade and microphone mute, with the display's own reports of changes made at the display.

help.overview: SMART Board RX and MX interactive displays over the RS-232 port: power, input, volume, mute, brightness, freeze, screen shade and the microphone mute. Changes made with the display's buttons, Settings app or remote reach OpenAVC as soon as they happen; everything is also read every 15 seconds while the display is on. Nothing is sent to the display while it reports Standby or Off, because any command would wake it.
help.setup:
1. Connect the display's RS-232 In port with a standard (straight-through)
   RS-232 cable, not a null-modem cable, to a serial port on this computer
   or to a serial bridge (choose "Through a bridge" and pick the bridge's
   port).
2. The settings are 19200 baud, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit. Through
   a bridge they are applied to the bridge's port for you.
3. No login. The display has no network control: RS-232 is the only way
   in.
help.connection: The display answers only while it is on or in Standby, and a command sent in Standby turns it on. After Turn Off it answers nothing until someone presses its Power button. Through a serial bridge, a display that stops answering while it reads On shows offline after three polls; on a direct serial port it stays connected.

compatible_models.notes: SMART Board RX series. Every command in this driver, including State Reporting and Factory Reset.
SMART Board MX (V5) and MX (V5) Pro. The same commands as the RX except State Reporting and Factory Reset, which its page does not list.

SMART Board MX (V2) to (V4) and their Pro models (discontinued). No HDMI 4, and the MX (V2) has one USB-C input; Turn Off is not available. They also take Screen Off (Ready) and Power Save, and report Updating while a software update runs. SMART asks for 30 seconds between power changes and the next command on iQ 3.11 or earlier.

drivers.name: SMART Board T Pro (Network)
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: SMART Board T Pro interactive displays over the network (TCP port 4664): power, input, volume, mute, the microphone array, the display's remote keys, and its picture, sound, touch and timer settings.

help.overview: SMART Board T Pro interactive displays over the network: power, input, volume, mute, the microphone array and the display's remote keys, plus treble, bass, balance, contrast, backlight, color temperature, language, speakers, touch, the screen timer, automatic brightness and the IR remote sensor as device settings. The display does not report changes by itself, so everything is read every 10 seconds.
help.setup:
1. Connect either of the display's RJ45 jacks to the network. On the
   display, press Input, tap Network, and note the IP address (reserve
   it in DHCP or set a static address). Ethernet must be Enabled in the
   display's Network settings.

2. Add the display here with that address. The port is 4664 and there
   is no login.

3. Keep the display out of Power Save. In Power Save the display does
   not answer on the network, and only its Power button, the remote or a
   video signal wakes it. Power Off (Ready) turns the screen off and keeps
   network control working.

4. Changing Eco mode turns the display's Ethernet off. After changing it
   at the display, turn Ethernet back on in the display's Network
   settings.

5. This driver is for network control. The display's RS-232 port uses a
   different set of commands.
help.connection: The display answers on the network while it is on or in Ready (screen off). In Power Save it answers nothing, so OpenAVC shows it offline until someone presses its Power button, uses the remote, or connects a video source.

compatible_models.notes: SMART Board T Pro series (IDT65-1 / IDT75-1 / IDT86-1). Network control on TCP 4664. The RS-232 port speaks a different protocol, which this driver does not use.

drivers.name: Sony Bravia Display
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Sony Bravia TVs and professional displays via the JSON-RPC REST API and IRCC remote emulation. Power, input, volume, mute, navigation, media transport, app launch. Covers Android TV, Google TV, and Pro Bravia models.

help.overview: Controls Sony Bravia displays using the built-in REST API and IRCC remote emulation. Works with Android TV, Google TV, and Pro Bravia series from ~2013 onwards (W, X, Z, A, XR models).
help.setup:
1. Connect the TV to the network.
2. On the TV, go to Settings > Network > Home Network Setup > IP Control.
3. Set Authentication to 'Normal and Pre-Shared Key'.
4. Set a Pre-Shared Key (e.g., '1234').
5. Set Simple IP Control to 'On' (enables power-on over network).
6. Enter the TV's IP address and PSK in the driver config.

compatible_models.notes: Verified on production hardware.

drivers.name: ViewSonic Commercial Display
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls ViewSonic CDE-series commercial displays, ViewBoard IFP62 and IFP110 interactive displays, and other ViewSonic large-format displays publishing the LFD RS-232 & LAN protocol, over the network (TCP port 5000, or 7142 on the IFP110) or direct RS-232. Power, input select, volume, mute, brightness, backlight, picture values, freeze and screen blank, PIP, video-wall tiling, keypad navigation, control locks, the display's clock, ambient sensor readings, and a Wake-on-LAN wake for displays whose standby closes the network port. Listens for the display's own status pushes and polls for the rest.

help.overview: ViewSonic commercial displays speaking the LFD RS-232 & LAN protocol. Power, input, audio, picture controls, screen blank and freeze, PIP, video-wall tiling, and control locks. The display pushes power / input / brightness / backlight / volume / mute changes on its own; everything else is polled every 30 seconds.
help.setup:
1. Network control: connect the display's LAN port, note the IP address
   from the network settings, and add it here (TCP port 5000, no
   login; 7142 on the ViewBoard IFP110). Monitor ID stays 1 for LAN control. On the CDE31 series,
   LAN Control must be On in the Advanced section of the display's
   on-screen menu.

2. Standby: on the CDE31 series set Power Save in the Advanced menu to
   Sleep. In Sleep the display keeps answering in standby, and Power On
   turns it on in about 3 seconds. In Hibernate it leaves the network
   about 6 seconds after Power Off and has to be turned on with its
   remote or power key. On other models, check the standby or
   network-standby setting the same way, or use Wake (Wake-on-LAN) for
   a model whose standby turns the network off (turn WOL on in the
   display's settings; the MAC address is learned on every connection).

3. Serial control: connect the display's RS-232 port (9-pin male) with a
   null-modem cable, or a straight cable plus the null-modem adapter
   that comes with the display, at 9600 8N1 (fixed). On the CDE31
   series turn RS232 On in the Advanced menu. On a daisy chain, set
   each display's Monitor ID in its menu and match it here.
help.connection: A display whose standby mode shuts the network down (Hibernate on the CDE31 series) does not answer on the network until it is turned on at the display. On models that wake over the network, Wake (Wake-on-LAN) turns it on; the display's MAC is learned automatically on every connection, or can be typed in under Edit Device for a display that has never connected.

compatible_models.notes: Verified on a CDE8631-1C over TCP 5000, on firmware 20250609234259 and 20260526125505. Set Power Save to Sleep in the Advanced menu for network control in standby and Power On; in Hibernate the display leaves the network, and it does not wake over Wake-on-LAN. Inputs: HDMI 1-3, USB-C, the embedded Android player, and the slot-in PC when one is installed. PIP, surround sound and the customized hot keys are not available on this model. Brightness, contrast and sharpness are refused while the embedded Android source is showing; use Backlight there.
The rest of the CDE31 series, documented in the same user guide as the verified CDE8631-1C. The slot-in PC input exists on 65-inch models and larger.

ViewBoard IFP62 series. Network control on TCP port 5000, or RS-232 at 9600 8N1 with a null-modem cable. Inputs: HDMI 1-3, VGA, the slot-in PC (OPS), DisplayPort, USB-C and the embedded Android player. Its own protocol page lists the set commands only; the status reads this driver polls come from ViewSonic's brand-wide protocol and are not yet checked on an IFP62.

ViewBoard IFP110. Network control on TCP port 7142: set TCP Port to 7142 when adding it. RS-232 at 9600 8N1 with a null-modem cable. Customized hot keys 1-7 open the ViewBoard apps (see Trigger Custom Hot Key).

The CDE30 and CDE20 series publish this protocol in their per-model RS-232 documentation. Every ViewSonic large-format display on the brand-wide LFD RS-232 & LAN protocol, including the other ViewBoard IFP interactive displays and NMP media players, is expected to work. Function support varies by model (PIP and tiling are model-dependent); an unsupported command answers a reject the driver ignores.
